original_alert.finding: Opened because cex-divergent-blaschke-sum cites it in F5 and step 3.1. Its Statement says 'A⊆Ω be discrete with multiplicities m(a)∈N' and promises 'whose zero at each a∈A has order exactly m(a)'. Two qualifications need checking: N includes zero in this library, so Ω=D, A={0}, m(0)=0 contradicts the literal requirement of a zero of order zero; also topological discreteness alone allows A={1/n:n≥2}⊂D, whose accumulation at 0 prevents the promised nonzero holomorphic function by the identity theorem. The proof assumes absence of accumulation throughout Ω, not merely isolation of points of A. The cited [Lebl text](https://www.jirka.org/ca/ca.pdf), Theorem 8.2.7, printed pp. 205–206, explicitly requires no limit points in the open set; its complete relevant proof was read. If 'discrete' is intended to mean locally finite here, that convention needs stating. The owned consumer uses an ambiently locally finite set and multiplicity one, so these boundary cases do not invalidate its particular application.
